es.summary: Hormona pancreática que eleva la glucosa plasmática al estimular la glucogenólisis hepática. Se administra por vía inyectable o spray nasal para tratar hipoglucemia grave y como inhibidor de la motilidad gastrointestinal.
key_points: Indicado para hipoglucemia severa cuando el paciente no puede ingerir glucosa oralmente.
Efecto rápido: aumento de glucosa en sangre en 10‑15 minutos.
Contraindicado en pacientes con feocromocitoma, insulinoma o hipersensibilidad conocida.
Reevaluar glucosa 15 minutos después de la dosis; repetir si <70 mg/dL.
Reacciones alérgicas graves (anafilaxia) y crisis hipertensiva son efectos serios.

mechanism: Se une a receptores hepáticos de glucagón, activando la adenilato ciclasa.
Aumenta cAMP, lo que estimula la glucogenólisis y gluconeogénesis.
Libera glucosa al torrente sanguíneo, elevando la concentración plasmática.
indications: Hipoglucemia grave en pacientes diabéticos (conciencia disminuida o incapacidad para ingerir azúcar).
Uso diagnóstico para inhibir la motilidad gastrointestinal durante estudios radiológicos.
contraindications: Hipersenibilidad conocida al glucagón o a sus excipientes.
adverse_effects: Dolor abdominal o sensación de plenitud.
interactions: Insulina: glucagón antagoniza su efecto, puede provocar hiperglucemia.
Betabloqueantes: pueden enmascarar los signos de hipoglucemia y reducir la respuesta al glucagón.
Agentes orales hipoglucemiantes: monitorizar glucosa para evitar fluctuaciones bruscas.
nursing_care: Verificar glucosa capilar <70 mg/dL y nivel de conciencia antes de administrar.
Confirmar ausencia de contraindicaciones (feocromocitoma, insulinoma, alergia).
Preparar dosis adecuada (0,5 mg adulto) y usar técnica aséptica.
Monitorear glucosa a los 15 min; repetir dosis si glucosa sigue <70 mg/dL.
Observar signos de reacción alérgica; notificar al médico si aparecen urticaria, dificultad respiratoria o presión arterial alta.
patient_teaching: Cómo usar el spray nasal: colocar en una fosa nasal y presionar el dispositivo una vez.
Instruir al cuidador sobre la técnica de inyección intramuscular/subcutánea de emergencia.
Reconocer síntomas de hipoglucemia (temblor, sudoración, confusión) y actuar inmediatamente.
Almacenar el glucagón a temperatura ambiente, proteger de la luz y no reutilizar viales abiertos.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de nivel de glucemia inestable
outcomes: Control de glucemia: mantener glucosa entre 70‑180 mg/dL en 24 h.
Reconocimiento de síntomas de hipoglucemia: identificar signos en menos de 5 min.

interventions.action: Evaluar glucosa capilar antes de cada administración de insulina o glucagón.
interventions.rationale: Detectar hipoglucemia precoz y prevenir eventos graves.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente y familia sobre signos de hipoglucemia y uso correcto del glucagón.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la intervención temprana y reduce complicaciones.

interventions.action: Mantener disponible kit de glucagón de emergencia en el hogar y en el trabajo.
interventions.rationale: Asegura acceso inmediato cuando el paciente no pueda ingerir glucosa.

interventions.action: Registrar y comunicar cualquier episodio de hipoglucemia al equipo de salud.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar el plan terapéutico y prevenir recurrencias.

interventions.action: Revisar y ajustar la dosis de insulina según patrones de glucosa y actividad física.
interventions.rationale: Optimiza el control glucémico y disminuye la necesidad de glucagón.

en.summary: Pancreatic hormone that raises plasma glucose by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis. It is administered via injectable or nasal spray to treat severe hypoglycemia and as a gastrointestinal motility inhibitor.
key_points: Indicated for severe hypoglycemia when the patient cannot ingest oral glucose.
Rapid effect: blood glucose rises within 10‑15 minutes.
Contraindicated in patients with pheochromocytoma, insulinoma, or known hypersensitivity.
Recheck glucose 15 minutes after dose; repeat if <70 mg/dL.
Serious adverse reactions include anaphylaxis and hypertensive crisis.

mechanism: Binds to hepatic glucagon receptors, activating adenylate cyclase.
Increases cAMP, stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Releases glucose into the bloodstream, raising plasma concentration.
indications: Severe hypoglycemia in diabetic patients (decreased consciousness or inability to ingest sugar).
Diagnostic use to inhibit gastrointestinal motility during radiologic studies.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to glucagon or its excipients.
interactions: Insulin: glucagon antagonizes its effect, may cause hyperglycemia.
Beta‑blockers: may mask signs of hypoglycemia and reduce response to glucagon.
Oral hypoglycemics: monitor glucose to avoid abrupt fluctuations.
nursing_care: Verify capillary glucose <70 mg/dL and level of consciousness before administration.
Confirm absence of contraindications (pheochromocytoma, insulinoma, allergy).
Prepare appropriate dose (0.5 mg adult) and use aseptic technique.
Monitor glucose at 15 min; repeat dose if glucose remains <70 mg/dL.
Observe for allergic reaction signs; notify physician if hives, respiratory difficulty, or high blood pressure occur.
patient_teaching: How to use the nasal spray: place in one nostril and press the device once.
Instruct caregiver on emergency intramuscular/subcutaneous injection technique.
Recognize hypoglycemia symptoms (tremor, sweating, confusion) and act immediately.
Store glucagon at room temperature, protect from light, and do not reuse opened vials.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for unstable blood glucose level
outcomes: Blood glucose control: maintain glucose between 70‑180 mg/dL within 24 h.
Recognition of hypoglycemia symptoms: identify signs within 5 min.

interventions.action: Assess capillary glucose before each insulin or glucagon administration.
interventions.rationale: Detect early hypoglycemia and prevent severe events.

interventions.action: Educate patient and family on hypoglycemia signs and correct glucagon use.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early intervention and reduces complications.

interventions.action: Keep an emergency glucagon kit available at home and work.
interventions.rationale: Ensures immediate access when patient cannot ingest glucose.

interventions.action: Document and communicate any hypoglycemia episode to the health team.
interventions.rationale: Allows adjustment of therapeutic plan and prevention of recurrences.

interventions.action: Review and adjust insulin dose based on glucose patterns and physical activity.
interventions.rationale: Optimizes glucose control and reduces need for glucagon.

summary.0.quote: Glucagon increases blood glucose levels by stimulating glycogen breakdown in the liver.

summary.1.quote: Glucagon comes as an injectable and as a nasal spray.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Glucagon increases blood glucose concentration by activating hepatic glucagon receptors, thereby stimulating glycogen breakdown and release of glucose from the liver.

sections.indications.1.quote: Glucagon for Injection is an antihypoglycemic agent and a gastrointestinal motility inhibitor indicated: • for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia in pediatric and adult patients with diabetes. ( 1.1 ) • as a diagnostic aid for use during radiologic examinations to temporarily inhibit movement of the gastrointestinal tract in adult patients.

sections.contraindications.0.quote: • Pheochromocytoma because of the risk of substantial increase in blood pressure [see Warning and Precautions (5.1) ]

sections.contraindications.1.quote: • Insulinoma because of the risk of hypoglycemia [see Warning and Precautions (5.2) ]

sections.contraindications.2.quote: • Known hypersensitivity to glucagon or to any of the excipients ( 4 )

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Allergic reactions, which have been reported with glucagon, may occur and include generalized rash, and in some cases anaphylactic shock with breathing difficulties, and hypotension.
